summary: Tested Office Roof Measurements two-way live-sync (auto-refresh polling + focus refresh + non-destructive dirty banner) on lead 5eed7c8d-b1b9-485b-b711-54d7d86260fc / measurement 0ad656d9-b09f-4ad8-8d0b-258b301f98af. Simulated Field edits via authenticated PUT /api/measurements/{id} with If-Match header (correctly converted response schema to ref-based payload). All 5 scenarios from the review request passed end-to-end.

test_results.clean_auto_adopt_polling: PASS - tot-area 1275SF -> 1386SF within 12s of field PUT (poll interval 15s)
test_results.dirty_banner_no_clobber: PASS - measurement-remote-update banner appeared in ~14s; local edit 'Main-EDITED-LOCAL' preserved; measurement-remote-update-dismiss hides banner and keeps local edits
test_results.banner_load_latest: PASS - measurement-remote-update-load loads server copy, clears dirty (save-btn hidden), banner disappears
test_results.window_focus_refresh: PASS - blur+focus triggered refresh in <0.5s (1518SF -> 1551SF), well before next 15s poll
test_results.normal_save_regression: PASS - dirty edit + measurement-save-btn click persists ('Main-SAVE-TEST' saved), 'Measurement saved' toast visible

critical_code_review_comments: MeasurementWorksheet.jsx is 552 lines - approaching the 700-line split threshold; the new live-sync block (~lines 109-152) is well-scoped, but the file overall could benefit from splitting Structures/Facets/Edges/Penetrations rows into subcomponents in a future refactor.
checkRemote() compares only updated_at strings for equality; that is fine given the server always writes fresh updated_at, but noting no fallback if timestamps ever have ms drift.
checkRemote() calls loadList() on every clean auto-adopt; harmless but an extra request per poll tick when a remote change lands (minor).
seed_data_creation: Reused existing lead 5eed7c8d-b1b9-485b-b711-54d7d86260fc + measurement 0ad656d9-b09f-4ad8-8d0b-258b301f98af. Mutated facet area_sqft and structure name during test (state modified but not reset).
context_for_next_testing_agent: When simulating a 'field' PUT to /api/measurements/{id}, the response schema is NOT the same as the PUT payload schema: server expects `ref` on structures/facets/edges/penetrations (existing UUIDs are treated as claims on rows owned by this revision) and `structure_ref`/`facet_ref` instead of `structure_id`/`facet_id`. Passing the GET response body verbatim yields 409 'referenced measurement item is stale'. The 5th regression scenario (stale-version 409 review flow with measurement-needs-review banner) was NOT re-exercised in this run since it's pre-existing behavior already verified in iterations 55-58 and unchanged by this diff.
